expected_effect: No action proposed. The verdict's named fix class (config_revert on payment) cannot be executed because its preconditions are not met by the evidence on this board: payment's 24-hour change history [tr_1778ce8ce3e6] contains only two platform-automation first-creation records (workload at 15:09:59, service object at 15:09:56) and no prior configuration state to restore, and no configuration or flag change is recorded for payment inside the incident window. The same holds for checkout [tr_d3518340b0ba]. Reverting payment to the only recorded prior configuration would mean reverting it to its creation-time state, which is the state it is already running — an action with no predicted observable effect on the 'Invalid token. app.loyalty.level=gold' rejection rate in payment's logs [tr_5d6996bcab13]. Furthermore, the suspected mechanism is a flag value held in the flagd store, which is not part of payment's own environment or configuration; recreating payment with reverted env would leave the flagd value untouched and the gold-tier rejections would resume on the first charge after restart. restart_service is also inappropriate: the evidence shows payment up, accepting traffic, and logging 'Charge request received.' through the end of the window [tr_407873775724], so this is not process state. The correct next step is a read of flagd's configuration and history to name the flag, its value, and its flip time — a diagnostic step, not a remediation this system is permitted to take.
if_wrong: This abstention is wrong if a flagd query (or a change-log query scoped to flagd rather than to payment) turns up a recorded prior configuration for payment naming a flag value inside 15:09–15:11, which would satisfy revert_config's two preconditions and make a config_revert on payment the right action. It is also wrong if payment's environment — not flagd's store — is where the failing-path toggle lives, in which case a revert would clear the rejections. Either finding should reopen this proposal immediately. Note that even a successful revert would be hard to confirm from metrics here: payment's error-ratio series has one defined sample and an empty baseline [tr_463410507be2], so confirmation would have to come from the cessation of the 'Invalid token. app.loyalty.level=gold' lines in payment's logs, which recur every 10–30s and so would be visible within about two minutes.
risk: The risk of abstaining is continued failure: gold-tier checkouts keep returning 'failed to charge card' to frontend and load-generator for as long as the flag stays flipped, at roughly one rejection every 10–30 seconds [tr_5d6996bcab13], with no self-healing observed through the end of the log window. The risk of acting instead would have been worse: revert_config recreates payment's container, so if the diagnosis is wrong the only effect is a connection-refused gap on the charge path — exactly the failure mode already seen once at ~15:10:56 in [tr_0d3e77248cba] — converting an attribute-segmented decline into a total payment outage for the recreate duration, while leaving the actual flag value in place.
blast_radius: No change is made, so nothing moves. Had the action been taken, it would have hit payment alone directly, with checkout seeing connection resets on Charge during the recreate, and frontend, frontend-proxy and load-generator seeing that propagate upward as the same 'failed to charge card' wrapper they already see. The thirteen services listed for this incident remain in their current state; the nine never directly examined are unaffected either way.
